incidents.vector: Scammers posing as a city contractor social-engineered staff over five months to change payment bank account details.
incidents.impact: The city wired $14.7 million to attacker-controlled accounts; the fraud was discovered about a week later when the real contractor reported a missing payment.

incidents.vector: Compromised developer devices (fake job interview and trojanized Homebrew download) yielded signing privileges, letting attackers flood a treasury wallet with 50 pre-signed EIP-7702 smart-account authorizations to install a malicious "sweeper" contract.
incidents.impact: Attackers transferred roughly $6.34 billion across at least 11 wallets before Binance froze and recovered about $2.85 billion; the FBI attributed the operation to North Korea's TraderTraitor group.

incidents.victim: Multiple organizations — semiconductor, defense, and civil-society sectors
incidents.vector: Chinese-speaking attackers (tracked as CL-STA-1238) paired the open-source Cairn AI pentesting framework with Chinese models GLM 5.2 and DeepSeek V4 to autonomously run 25 reconnaissance-to-exploitation operations with minimal human input.
incidents.impact: Confirmed unauthorized access or data theft at 10 of 19 targeted organizations, including mass exposure of over a million records at a teachers' union, persistent admin accounts at a semiconductor maker, and tampering with a live industry standards-ballot document.

incidents.vector: A worm-like toolkit (SCKit) abused a third-party ScreenConnect extension (RMM+) with a default-blank authentication key to push rogue remote-access clients to managed endpoints, bypassing MFA.
incidents.impact: 288 endpoints across 48 organizations were reached within 90 minutes; attackers installed persistent backdoors and positioned to hijack operator sessions, though session-hijack attempts failed in logs reviewed so far.

incidents.victim: Government ministries — one Middle Eastern and four Southeast Asian countries
incidents.vector: Attackers planted malicious JavaScript on webmail portals and government web applications to run the "Falcon" (XG) browser-based C2 framework, sideloading malicious Chrome extensions and delivering the Antino implant via Microsoft OneDrive.
incidents.impact: Compromised browser sessions at ministries of foreign affairs, defense, interior, and law enforcement agencies, stealing passwords, emails, session cookies, and communications between March and May 2026.

incidents.victim: Multiple financially motivated ransomware victims (TAG-218 / Settra)
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited VPN appliances (SonicWall, Palo Alto Networks, Fortinet) for initial access, then deployed the previously undocumented "GhostFrame" post-exploitation framework on compromised VMware ESXi hosts to harvest credentials and pivot across virtual machines.
incidents.impact: At least four victimized organizations have appeared on the Settra ransomware leak site; GhostFrame gives operators centralized control, credential harvesting, and network-pivoting across entire virtualized environments from a single compromised hypervisor.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached the company's drone flight-planning software and planted a malicious update.
incidents.impact: Quantum Systems, a supplier of drones to the Ukrainian military, shut down its IT network and German defense forces grounded UAVs while the company investigated; the malicious file was reportedly never delivered to any drones in the field.

incidents.victim: ActiveCloud, ESTT, and Beget (Belarusian and Russian cloud hosting providers)
incidents.vector: Unidentified attackers breached infrastructure management systems at three regional cloud hosting providers; at Beget, hackers deployed scripts that wiped data from parts of the cloud environment, while ActiveCloud and ESTT suffered ransomware-style encryption of services.
incidents.impact: Disruption to corporate websites, email, and virtual servers for businesses, news outlets, and government agencies across Belarus and Russia; Beget lost some virtual server backups, complicating recovery. No group has claimed responsibility and no link between the three incidents has been publicly confirmed.

incidents.vector: The BYOD ransomware group, active since September 2026, breached Vanderbilt's network, forcing the university to order a shutdown of devices and campus WiFi while it investigated and contained the intrusion.
incidents.impact: BYOD claims to have stolen more than one million Social Security numbers belonging to students and staff; the group has separately hit Michigan State University and the University of New Mexico in recent weeks.

incidents.vector: Attackers gained access to Expedia's network through a third-party data platform provider.
incidents.impact: The n0n data extortion group leaked Expedia data online after the company refused to pay a ransom; Expedia is the world's second-largest travel agency by revenue.

incidents.vector: An attacker used a forgotten cloud access key, originally issued to a third-party AI service provider, to enter Barracuda's cloud environment and then deployed the ARTEX AI penetration-testing framework to escalate access across internal networks and other cloud environments.
incidents.impact: The intruder reached roughly 10 cloud environments over nearly two days, including some managing Barracuda's XDR platform, and searched for crypto-wallet seed phrases and secrets; Barracuda found no evidence customer XDR credentials were accessed.

incidents.victim: Multiple organizations — financial services, retail, technology, transportation (North America, South America, APAC)
incidents.vector: Threat actors including UNC6993 used exposed cloud identity tokens, stolen API keys, and a LiteLLM gateway vulnerability (CVE-2026-40217) to hijack enterprise LLM access ("LLMJacking") and resell stolen capacity through illicit "LLM Mixer" routing gateways.
incidents.impact: Individual incidents generated fraudulent cloud charges exceeding $100,000 in a single day, with cumulative charges at some organizations reaching $1 million before access was revoked.

incidents.victim: 1.3 million Android TV set-top boxes and other IoT devices (global)
incidents.vector: Chinese device manufacturer Videostrong Technology preloaded firmware-level backdoor malware (XCPE) on TV boxes and other Android IoT devices, then sold affiliate access so criminal groups could load ad-fraud and residential-proxy modules.
incidents.impact: Google and industry partners dismantled the botnet, which enrolled over 1.3 million devices and is expected to sever access to at least 10 million more; Google banned Videostrong from the certified Android device program.

incidents.victim: Hundreds of European supermarkets and some medical facilities
incidents.vector: Attackers gained unauthorized access to internet-exposed refrigeration controllers, likely via vulnerable software or default credentials, and set units to defrost mode, in some cases raising temperatures to 50°C (122°F).
incidents.impact: Roughly 700 French supermarkets lost power to refrigeration in an October wave, followed by a November wave hitting 100-115 more locations across 10+ European countries, causing spoiled food, some fires, and impact to medical facility refrigeration; French authorities formally attributed the attacks to Iran's IRGC, though pro-Russian hacktivist groups NoName057(16) and Z-Pentest had separately claimed responsibility.

incidents.vector: An attacker stole an access key Cursor had issued to AI training platform Fireworks.ai and used it to upload a trojanized version of Anthropic's official Claude Code extension to the Cursor marketplace.
incidents.impact: The malicious extension installed SSH backdoors on roughly 5,000 systems; the broader Fireworks.ai breach also exposed customer data, leading Uber to notify drivers their data was stolen.

incidents.vector: Attackers chained the PHP2Shell remote code execution vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) with a DynamicCLI privilege-escalation flaw (CVE-2026-123039) to drop a web shell on Check Point Security Gateways.
incidents.impact: Following the initial web shell, attackers deployed a proxy, a wiper, and other components on compromised gateways; exploitation began in late October, about a week after patches were released.

incidents.vector: Storm-0940, assessed as a China-state-aligned actor, compromised ConnectWise application credentials and used the ARTEX AI penetration-testing framework to automate sign-in attempts against downstream Microsoft 365 tenants.
incidents.impact: The campaign accelerated sign-in attempts against more than 2,250 downstream Microsoft 365 tenants, with follow-on activity involving Microsoft Graph abuse, application credential theft, and privilege changes.
